pairs.subject: data-retention
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/retention.rs:343 The artifact purge walks the whole delete list in one unbounded pass. It has no time budget, no batching and no partial or out-of-budget outcome. It returns a bare (files, bytes) tuple, so a failed delete cannot reach the run's status, and the configurable age window that drives it has no floor.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/retention.rs:38 The preview is a mode of the deleter: plan_artifact_retention is pure, and the server preview and the janitor both call the same artifact_retention_plan. The four keep/reclaim classes partition the tree per app. Gap: RetentionPlan carries no cutoff moment and no as-of timestamp (count-carries-predicate). The preview emits only cutoff_days.

crates/core/src/retention.rs:357 A per-file failure goes only to a log line and never enters the result, so the janitor reports Ran while some deletes failed (degraded shows as green). There is no budget derived from a runner limit and no batch boundary. The sibling HealthStore::prune (crates/core/src/resilience/store.rs:703) is a single unbounded DELETE statement.

crates/core/src/retention.rs:202 The cutoff predicate accepts any window. Config validation (config.rs:1100-1135) checks only cross-key consistency, so artifact_retention_days = 1 is accepted and deletes every unpinned body older than a day, unattended. No floor refuses it, and there is no out-of-band opt-in. HealthStore::prune also clamps keep.max(1) (store.rs:694) rather than refusing. The 0 = off sentinel is honoured; the pin veto mitigates but is not a floor.

crates/core/src/retention.rs:210 This is a single-deployment, local-first service: the plan takes one global cutoff with no tenant dimension. The technique's 'single-tenant systems' exclusion applies. The keep-everything sentinel (0 = off, the default) does exist in config.

crates/core/src/retention.rs:343 The only caller is the unattended janitor, and the server exposes only GET /retention/preview. No operator-initiated destructive retention operation exists, so the technique's 'unattended paths' exclusion applies.

crates/core/src/retention.rs:22 Deletion here is horizon-only over scraped bodies and health sketches. A search of crates/ for erasure, gdpr and 'data subject' found nothing, and no subject-erasure obligation is declared. Low confidence: scraped content could contain personal data.
